transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Um, thank you for seeing me. I hope I'm in the right place. I'm just here because... well, I feel like I'm always running a little hot, you know? Like I can't quite shut the motor off. Which is usually fine! It makes me a hard worker. But lately, I guess, maybe it's been getting me into a little bit of trouble at the firehouse. Nothing too crazy, I don't think, but... enough that I thought I should probably get it checked out. Is that the kind of thing you help people with?

When you say you're 'running a little hot' and can't shut the motor off — does this feel like it's been pretty much the same all the time, or do you have periods where it's much more intense than other times?

Um, I think it's pretty much just... the same all the time? Yeah, it's always just kind of there. I don't really have, like, extreme spikes where it's way worse or anything. It's just a steady... a steady hum, I guess. 

Which, honestly, I always thought was a good thing! It keeps me on my toes, you know? I'm always ready to jump on a call at the station. So it's not like I'm losing control or having these crazy episodes or anything scary... it's just my normal baseline. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering that right.
Going back to when you were a kid — were you always like this? Like, did your parents or teachers ever say you were hyperactive or had trouble sitting still, even back then?

Um, yeah, I guess so. My mom actually brought that up recently. She said I was... well, she said I was pretty much exactly like this back in grade school, too. 

I mean, I wasn't a bad kid or anything! I just... I had a lot of energy. She said I was always out of my seat, and I guess I had a habit of blurting out answers before the teacher called on me. Just getting a little too excited, you know? And, um, I'd lose my homework sometimes, which meant I got a few notes sent home. But my teachers always said I was bright enough to do the work, so it wasn't like I was failing or anything. It was just a little... disorganized, maybe? I hope that doesn't sound too terrible. I really did try to be a good student.

When you're trying to focus on something — like reading a report or listening to someone explain instructions — do you find it hard to concentrate, or does your mind tend to wander? Or is it more that you just have trouble sitting still?

Um, well... I guess it's a little bit of both? But maybe more the mind-wandering thing. I mean, I really do try to pay attention! Especially because the stuff we do is important. 

Like, when we have briefings, or... lately I've been doing this drone training for search and rescue, which is really cool. And I'm totally locked in for the first few minutes, you know? I'm right there. But then... I don't know, I'll realize I've just been staring at the map or the screen for a while, and I completely missed like half of what command just went over. 

It's not that I don't care, I promise. I really want to hear it. It's just like my brain sort of... slips a gear, maybe? I always make sure to double-check with the other guys afterward so I don't mess anything up, so it hasn't caused any real disasters. But, yeah, sitting still and just listening to a long explanation can be kind of tough for me. Is that... is that pretty common for people? I hope I'm not the only one who does that.

You mentioned blurting out answers in class — do you find yourself doing impulsive things now, like interrupting people, making quick decisions without thinking them through, or acting on urges without considering the consequences?

Um, well... I wouldn't say I do anything really reckless or, like, make crazy decisions without thinking. I'm actually pretty careful on the job! But, um... I guess maybe the interrupting thing still happens a little bit? 

It's really just because I get so focused on solving the problem, you know? Like, if we're at the station and the guys are talking through a plan or trying to figure out how to tackle something, and I already see the answer in my head... I just kind of jump in. I don't mean to be rude or anything! I just want to help get us there faster. But then, after I do it, I'll realize I totally stepped on somebody's sentence or kind of messed up the whole flow of the discussion. 

I always feel really bad about it afterward, and I try to apologize. I just get a little too eager to help, I think. Does that make sense? I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible team player, because I really do respect the other guys a lot.

Have you ever had a period — maybe lasting a few days or longer — where you felt noticeably more energetic, more confident, or like you needed less sleep than usual, and it felt like a real change from your normal baseline? Or has it always just been this steady hum you've described?

Um, no... no, I don't think I've ever had anything quite like that. Like a sudden change where I stop sleeping for days? No, it's really just always been this... this steady hum, exactly like you said. 

I mean, I really try to make sure I get my rest, especially because the guys at the station depend on me. I wouldn't want to show up to a call completely exhausted or acting totally out of character, you know? So I don't get these big, dramatic shifts where I suddenly feel invincible or anything. It's just my normal, everyday level of... well, being a little restless, I guess. 

I hope that's okay? Like, I hope it's a good thing that I'm at least pretty consistent with it. I definitely don't want to sound like I'm completely all over the place.

When you're managing your responsibilities — like keeping track of your schedule, organizing your gear, paying bills, or keeping your living space in order — do you find yourself struggling with that kind of stuff? Or does that come pretty naturally to you?

Um, well... I try really hard to keep everything organized. I really do. I don't want you to think my life is a total mess or anything, because I usually manage to get things done eventually! 

But, um... I guess I do struggle a little bit with remembering the smaller details? It's just... I keep forgetting stuff that I honestly, truly mean to do. Like, I'll completely intend to sign off on my training modules at the station, or call people back, and it just... poof, it's gone from my brain. Or, um, sometimes I might not pay a bill until the late fee hits, which is really embarrassing to admit. Or I'll forget to bring the right gear paperwork in on shift.

I always apologize to the captain when that happens, and I fix it right away! I really don't want to be a burden on anyone, and I know how important that paperwork is. I just... I don't know why those things slip past me when I'm trying so hard to keep track of them. I hope that doesn't make me sound completely irresponsible? I really am trying my best to stay on top of it all. Is it... is it normal to struggle with that kind of stuff even when you're really trying?

When you're at the firehouse or doing your drone training, how much would you say these things — the mind wandering, the interrupting, forgetting tasks — are actually getting in the way of doing your job well, or causing problems with your relationships with the other firefighters?

Um, well... I mean, I really don't want to make it sound like I'm doing a terrible job, because I do love being a firefighter and I care about the crew so much. But, um... I guess it is starting to become a bit of an issue? 

I, uh... I actually got pulled into a performance and safety meeting recently. Which was really hard to hear, because I always want to be someone the guys can rely on, you know? But they were saying that because I keep missing the little details, or, you know, forgetting the paperwork, it's... it's starting to affect how much they trust me on the job. 

And, um, I was really hoping to move up into a leadership role soon, but now it feels like that's kind of slipping away. They just... they need to know they can count on me to track everything consistently, and right now, I guess I'm not doing a great job of showing them that. 

I'm really trying to fix it, though! I promised them I'd do better. It's just... it's really discouraging when you're trying so hard and it still isn't enough. I hope you don't think less of me for that? I really am committed to being a good firefighter and a good teammate. I just... I really want to figure out how to get back on track.
Has anyone ever diagnosed you with ADHD or attention deficit disorder, either when you were a kid or as an adult? Or has a doctor ever suggested that might be something to look into?

Um, no... no one has ever really brought that up before. I mean, not a doctor or anything. 

When I was a kid, my teachers would sometimes say I had a lot of energy, or that I needed to apply myself more, but they never used those words. They just said I was a spirited kid, which... I guess is a nice way of putting it? My parents just figured I was an active boy who liked being outside more than sitting at a desk. 

And as an adult, I've always just tried to push through it and work harder. I really didn't want to be the kind of person who makes excuses, you know? I always thought if I just tried a little more, or cared a little more, I could get it all under control. So I never actually asked a doctor about it until now. 

I hope it's okay that I waited this long to look into it? I really wasn't trying to ignore a problem, I just... I honestly thought it was a personal failing I needed to fix on my own. I hope you don't think I'm silly for not realizing it sooner.
